`--max-columns=abc` is parsed by `parseArgs`. When the argument starts with `max-columns=`, it passes the text after the `=` to `parseCount` (src/main.zig:1187-1188).

`parseCount` calls `std.fmt.parseInt(usize, value, 10)` and turns any error into `null` (src/main.zig:813-815). Since `"abc"` isn't a valid base-10 unsigned integer, it returns `null`.

The `orelse` branch then sets `opts.fail = .{ .what = "bad value for --max-columns", .arg = "abc" }` and returns `error.Usage` (src/main.zig:1188-1190). The user gets a usage error with the message "bad value for --max-columns" and the offending argument `abc`.

The context doesn't show how `opts.fail` is printed, so the exact output text and the exit code aren't confirmed here. The `--max-columns abc` (separate-argument) form is handled the same way (src/main.zig:1198-1200).
